title: MEL-Code: Transferring Meta-Experience Learning to Code RLVR with Unit-Test Rewards

contributions.purpose: Enable Meta-Experience Learning, previously limited to mathematical reasoning, to work in code generation RLVR where solutions may differ from the first line.
contributions.mechanism: A three-stage pipeline (contrastive pair construction from GRPO rollouts, replay validation via unit-test re-execution, NLL internalization) with template-based meta-experience construction suited to the code domain.
contributions.evaluation: Validated on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with MBPP training, achieving highest MBPP performance and 33% faster convergence than baselines.
contributions.source_quote: A three-stage pipeline adapting MEL to code RLVR, with template-based meta-experience construction suited to the code domain where solutions may differ from the first line.

contributions.purpose: Establish whether code RLVR naturally produces enough contrastive signal for meta-experience learning.
contributions.mechanism: Measurement of usable contrastive pair yield across GRPO training prompts during code RLVR training.
contributions.evaluation: 66% of training prompts yield usable contrastive pairs, far exceeding the 5% threshold reported for math MEL.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical validation that code RLVR generates abundant meta-experience signal, with 66% of training prompts yielding usable contrastive pairs—far exceeding the 5% threshold from math MEL.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that internalized meta-experiences improve code-generation performance and training efficiency.
contributions.mechanism: MEL-Code training compared against baselines, with ablation studies isolating each pipeline stage.
contributions.evaluation: 9.2% vs. 8.8% greedy Pass@1 on MBPP and 33% faster convergence; ablations show replay validation is the most critical component.
contributions.source_quote: Demonstration of improved MBPP performance (9.2% vs. 8.8% greedy Pass@1) and 33% faster convergence, with ablation studies showing replay validation as the most critical component.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We present MEL-Code, which transfers Meta-Experience Learning to code RLVR with unit-test rewards.

MEL has demonstrated consistent improvements of 3.9–4.7% Pass@1 on math benchmarks. However, its applicability to code generation remains unexplored, as code solutions may lack the stepwise structure of mathematical proofs and unit-test feedback differs fundamentally from answer verification.
Our work differs by focusing on contrastive pairs of complete solutions rather than step-level rewards, leveraging the natural structure of unit-test feedback to construct meta-experiences.

notes: Partial negative-result paper: abstract states gains are domain-specific and meta-experiences learned from MBPP do not transfer to HumanEval+. The headline MBPP gain is small (9.2% vs 8.8% greedy Pass@1).
